name: test-glsl-language
title: GLSL ES language rules at run time
summary: GLSL ES 1.00 shaders (attribute/varying/gl_FragColor/gl_FragData, a shader without #version, texture2D/texture2DProj/textureCube, texture2DLod/texture2DProjLod/textureCubeLod in the vertex shader, the fragment-only bias) rendered on an ES 3.x context and compared with a CPU reference; linking across language versions fails; operators, parameter passing (copy-in/copy-out, aliasing, evaluation order), constant folding and scoping evaluated in both the vertex language (transform feedback) and the fragment language (four RGBA32UI attachments) and compared bit-exactly or under the §4.5.1 precision rules; gl_Max* constants are at least the specified minimums in both languages (3.00 §7.3, 3.10 §7.2 on ES >= 3.1) and gl_MaxVertexUniformVectors equals MAX_VERTEX_UNIFORM_VECTORS in GLSL ES 1.00 and 3.00 (§1.5); equality of the other constants with the API limits is reported, not asserted; gl_DepthRange equals the clamped glDepthRangef values; invariant gl_Position and #pragma STDGL invariant(all) outputs are bit-identical across programs; a constant expression is bit-identical in both languages.
spec: GLSL ES 1.00 §3.4 (#version), §4.3.3 Attribute, §4.3.5 Varying, §7.2 Fragment Shader Special Variables, §8.7 Texture Lookup Functions
GLSL ES 3.00 §1.5 Compatibility, §3.1 Logical Phases of Compilation, §3.4 Version Declaration, §3.6 Comments, §3.8 Keywords
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.1.3 Integers, §4.2 Scoping, §4.3.2 Constant Qualifier, §4.3.3 Constant Expressions, §4.5.1 Range and Precision
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.6 Variance and the Invariant Qualifier (§4.6.1, §4.6.3)
GLSL ES 3.00 §5.1 Operators, §5.7 Structure and Array Operations, §5.8 Assignments, §5.9 Expressions, §5.10 Vector and Matrix Operations
GLSL ES 3.00 §6.1 Function Definitions, §6.1.1 Function Calling Conventions
GLSL ES 3.00 §1.5 Compatibility (gl_MaxVertexUniformVectors), §7.3 Built-In Constants (minimums), §7.4 Built-In Uniform State
GLSL ES 3.10 §3.3 Version Declaration, §7.2 Built-In Constants (minimums); GLSL ES 1.00 §7.4 Built-In Constants

ES 3.0 §2.12.3 Program Objects (link), §2.13.1 Controlling the Viewport (DepthRangef clamping), §2.15 Transform Feedback, §3.8.10 Texture Minification (lambda, bias, mipmap level), §4.2.1 Selecting Buffers for Writing, §4.3.1 Reading Pixels

api.glBindAttribLocation: GLSL ES 1.00 attributes bound to locations 0/1/2 before linking; the rendered gradient and texture lookups prove the binding
api.glLinkProgram: LINK_STATUS FALSE for 100+300 es, 300 es+100, 310 es+300 es, 300 es+310 es, 310 es+100; TRUE for the same-version positive controls
api.glTransformFeedbackVaryings: four flat uvec4 outputs (or gl_Position / v_res for the invariance programs) captured interleaved
api.glBeginTransformFeedback: POINTS capture with RASTERIZER_DISCARD; captured words compared with CPU references
api.glEndTransformFeedback: capture completes before the buffer is mapped
api.glMapBufferRange: MAP_READ_BIT readback of the captured words
api.glDrawBuffers: four RGBA32UI attachments receive layout(location = 0..3) fragment outputs; each is read back
api.glClearBufferuiv: sentinel 0xCDCDCDCD per attachment, overwritten by every fragment case
api.glReadBuffer: selects COLOR_ATTACHMENT0..3 for the integer readback
api.glReadPixels: RGBA_INTEGER / UNSIGNED_INT readback of the fragment results; RGBA / UNSIGNED_BYTE probes of the GLSL ES 1.00 picture
api.glDepthRangef: values clamped to [0, 1] seen as gl_DepthRange.near/far/diff in both languages
api.glGetFloatv: DEPTH_RANGE equals the clamped glDepthRangef arguments
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_VERTEX_UNIFORM_VECTORS asserted equal to gl_MaxVertexUniformVectors (GLSL ES 3.00 §1.5, in 1.00 and 3.00 shaders); the other limits are only printed next to their gl_Max* constants

visual_review.notes: Viewed gpu es-max 256x256 and llvmpipe 333x777. Bottom row: affine gradient (blue bottom-left, red bottom-right, cyan top-left, yellow top-right), the 4x4 texture drawn by the shader without #version, and the same texture twice through texture2DProj vec3 and vec4. Top row: six cube faces (red, green, blue; yellow, magenta, cyan), vertex-shader LOD draws (red, green, yellow; blue, green, cyan), bias halves red and green. Every cell fills its share of the surface.
